summary: Select largest vertex-count segment at exact contour level and parse its orientation/endpoints

capability: Select the largest-vertex-count contour segment at an exact level and parse its orientation and endpoints.
operation: contour set, exact level and optional endpoint/orientation controls -> selected parsed vertices
discovery.model: Contour-segment selection with the nearest-endpoint convention from segment parsing; idx_check is an ignored compatibility argument and no field is reconstructed.
discovery.geometry: Planar contour-set segments with ordered vertices in caller length units and exact level labels in caller flux-label units.
discovery.boundary: The requested level must exactly appear in the contour levels and at least one finite segment must exist; unique physical flux surfaces and connections between separate segments are not established.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to Selected parsed vertices
identity.definition: Select largest vertex-count segment at exact contour level and parse its orientation/endpoints
identity.model: Source contour segment selection; idx_check is ignored compatibility argument
identity.coordinates: Planar segment vertices and exact level labels
assumptions: Requested level exactly appears in contourset.levels
At least one finite segment exists

inputs.name: contourset
inputs.units: levels in caller flux-label units; vertices length
inputs.constraints: Each allsegs entry contains finite planar segments

inputs.name: end_coord
inputs.description: Nearest terminal coordinate included in output
inputs.constraints: Terminal vertex retained; no interpolated crossing

outputs.name: segment
outputs.constraints: Largest segment selected by original point count

preconditions: Requested level exactly appears in contourset.levels
At least one finite segment exists
supported: Finite inputs satisfying the callable-specific shape, support, and boundary conditions
excluded: Does not establish unique physical flux surface or connect separate segments

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError or the underlying NumPy/SciPy exception for nonfinite, mismatched, unsorted, out-of-domain, or malformed inputs; no input repair is inferred.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical, interpolation, or optional-dependency exceptions propagate from the direct calculation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the relation uses direct finite-difference, interpolation, selection, or quadrature operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is promised when input validation or the underlying numerical operation fails.

python.signature: get_fieldlines(contourset, level, start_coord=None, end_coord=None, clockwise=True, idx_check=[])

example.description: Select the available contour segment at an exact level and return its vertices.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from types import SimpleNamespace
from scirel.geometry.sampling import get_fieldlines

segment = np.array([[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0], [1.0, 0.0]])
contours = SimpleNamespace(levels=[0.2], allsegs=[[segment]])
selected = get_fieldlines(contours, 0.2)
assert selected.shape == (4, 2)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(selected, segment)
example.expected: The selected contour has shape (4, 2) and retains the four vertices.
